name: Ipomoea

project_scope.taxonomic_note: The source-pool row Ipomoea cordatotriloba var. cordatotriloba is taught inside canonical Ipomoea cordatotriloba rather than duplicated. Current Kew/POWO accepts I. cordatotriloba at species rank; ITIS/GRIN retain the autonym as an accepted/recognized infraspecific treatment. The project preserves the source name but uses one learner card. Distimake dissectus is intentionally outside this genus folder.

high_value_diagnostics: sepal length, shape, awns/tips, and pubescence

quick_comparison.hederacea: long 12–24 mm sepals with very long narrow curved/spreading tips
quick_comparison.cordatotriloba: pink-purple flower, ciliate ~8–12 mm sepals, variable cordate/3-lobed leaves; var. cordatotriloba source row is represented here
quick_comparison.lindheimeri: large blue-violet flower, palmately lobed hairy leaves, 18–30 mm sepals
quick_comparison.nil: very large blue/purple flower, large hairy cordate/3-lobed leaves
quick_comparison.lacunosa: small white flower, 11–14 mm acuminate sepals
quick_comparison.coccinea: small scarlet flower, sepals with subterminal awnlike projection
quick_comparison.batatas: cultivated/escaped sweet potato comparison; use swollen storage roots plus broader crop-context characters rather than treating it as a native morning-glory anchor

curation_status.photo_rights: all images retain exact canonical image source/license/creator; private-study and noncommercial images NOT promoted

source_concept_status.learner_action: teach as source/infraspecific name inside I. cordatotriloba; no duplicate page

diagnostic_science_handoff.first_look: Measure corolla length and both outer and inner sepal lengths on a flowering specimen; inspect sepal tips and hairs before using leaf lobing or flower color.
diagnostic_science_handoff.triloba_vs_cordatotriloba: I. triloba usually has a 15–20 mm corolla and 5–8 mm sepals; I. cordatotriloba has a 25–40 mm corolla, 8–11 mm outer sepals, and 10–12 mm inner sepals. Values approach/overlap at the sepal boundary. Leaf lobing is variable in both.
diagnostic_science_handoff.hederacea_vs_nil: I. hederacea has elongated tapering sepals (15–25 mm in Go Botany). I. nil has overlapping leaf lobing and flower appearance; verify sepals on the actual specimen before deciding.
required_photos: outer and inner sepals with scale
diagnostic_science_handoff.boundary: Review only. Do not create canonical taxa or READY markers. Preserve existing learner admission and native-range states.

look_here_first_sequence: Start with the flower in side view and estimate/measure corolla length.
Measure outer and inner sepals; inspect whether their distal portions are short, gradually tapered, abruptly narrowed, curved/recurved, or awned.
Check sepal/peduncle pubescence and whether pedicels are erect or reflexed where relevant.
Only then use leaf lobing, leaf hairiness, annual/perennial habit, and rooting/storage organs as supporting characters.
Use fruit/seed characters when flowers are absent or when lacunosa-complex plants remain ambiguous.

comparison_matrix.sepals: 6–7 mm in FNA; short, ciliate, acute/obtuse and mucronulate-caudate
comparison_matrix.support: Annual; leaves entire to 3–7-lobed; peduncles generally glabrous
comparison_matrix.strongest_separator: Much shorter sepals and smaller flower than I. hederacea, I. nil, I. lindheimeri; usually smaller than I. cordatotriloba

comparison_matrix.corolla: 20–38 mm in FNA, lavender with darker tube
comparison_matrix.sepals: 8–14 mm; outer lance-ovate/lanceolate, inner ovate; ciliate/hairy or glabrous depending variety
comparison_matrix.support: Perennial twiner; leaf shape highly variable; foliage often hairy but var. torreyana can be glabrous
comparison_matrix.strongest_separator: Intermediate flower/sepal size plus perennial habit; lacks the exaggerated sepal form of I. hederacea

comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Abruptly narrowed, long curved/spreading sepal tips
comparison_matrix.corolla: 20–37(–45) mm, usually light blue with pale tube
comparison_matrix.sepals: 12–24 mm; proximally broader then abruptly narrowed into a long curved/spreading distal portion; basal part hirsute/hispid
comparison_matrix.support: Annual; hairy foliage; retrorsely hairy peduncles
comparison_matrix.strongest_separator: Sepal shape is more useful than leaf shape; compare directly with I. nil

comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Large flower + long, densely hairy, gradually tapered sepals
comparison_matrix.corolla: (20–)30–60+ mm in FNA, usually blue to purplish
comparison_matrix.sepals: 15–25(–30) mm; lance-linear, densely hispid basally, gradually narrowed to a straighter distal portion
comparison_matrix.strongest_separator: Against I. hederacea, use gradual/straighter sepal taper plus usually larger corolla—not leaf lobing

comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Small white flower + acuminate medium-length sepals
comparison_matrix.sepals: (8–)11–14 mm; elliptic-oblong to lanceolate/lance-ovate; ciliate margins, acuminate apex, surfaces glabrous
comparison_matrix.support: Annual; leaves entire or 3(–5)-lobed; fruit 10–13 mm diameter
comparison_matrix.strongest_separator: White corolla with acuminate 11–14 mm sepals; watch the I. ×leucantha hybrid trap

comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Very large blue-violet flower + very long hairy sepals
comparison_matrix.sepals: 18–30 mm, lanceolate to lance-ovate, usually hispid
comparison_matrix.support: Perennial; usually 3–5(–7)-lobed hairy leaves; shaggy retrorsely hairy peduncles
comparison_matrix.strongest_separator: Extreme flower size plus long sepals and perennial/rootstock habit

comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Corniform/awnlike sepal appendages + reflexed fruiting pedicels
comparison_matrix.corolla: 20–25 mm, usually red or red-and-yellow, salverform
comparison_matrix.sepals: Outer 3–3.5 mm and inner 4.5–5.7 mm, each with a terminal corniform appendage
comparison_matrix.support: Annual; peduncles glabrous; leaves usually cordate; pedicels become reflexed beneath the fruit
comparison_matrix.strongest_separator: From I. hederifolia, reflexed fruiting pedicels plus larger inner sepals are stronger than red flower alone

comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Tuberlike storage root + trailing crop/escape habit
comparison_matrix.corolla: (30–)40–70 mm, lavender/pink/purplish or white with darker throat
comparison_matrix.support: Perennial; root relatively large and tuberlike; stems usually trailing, rarely twining; leaves cordate to 5–7-lobed
comparison_matrix.strongest_separator: Storage root and crop/escaped habit; foliage is too variable to use alone

comparison_cautions: Leaf shape is highly variable across the genus and should be supporting evidence, not the first decision point.
I. triloba and I. cordatotriloba overlap in leaf lobing and approach one another in sepal size; flower size plus the full sepal suite is stronger.
I. hederacea and I. nil overlap in sepal length. The shape of the distal sepal portion—abrupt/curved versus more gradual/straight—matters more than a single measurement.
I. lacunosa can hybridize with I. cordatotriloba to form I. ×leucantha; use corolla/fruit/seed size and the whole character suite when a white/lavender small-flowered plant looks intermediate.
Red flowers do not by themselves prove I. coccinea; compare the corniform sepal appendages and fruiting-pedicel posture against I. hederifolia.

Foreground the verified anatomy of nil sepals, the variable lobed foliage, flower folds, and honest missing diagnostic ruler macros.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Start SIDE-ON: COROLLA length and FIVE SEPALS. TRILOBA small (corolla 10–20 mm; sepals ~6–7 mm) → CORDATOTRILOBA larger (20–38; sepals 8–14) → HEDERACEA long curved-point sepals → NIL longer gradual hairy sepals → LINDHEIMERI huge flower. LACUNOSA is small white and hybrid caution; COCCINEA red small and hornlike sepals; BATATAS crop with storage root.

look_here_first: SEE: observe the whole vine, COROLLA and foliage. SPOT: turn a fresh flower SIDEWAYS and expose all FIVE SEPARATE SEPALS (the green parts below the COROLLA), especially their tips and hairs. NAME: compare corolla length AND exact outer/inner SEPAL length, form, pubescence and pedicel orientation against the four key local pairs (triloba/cordatotriloba; hederacea/nil; lacunosa/×leucantha; coccinea/hederifolia). COMPARE: use full leaf outlines, flower count, rootstock and mature fruit/seed as backup; leaf lobing or color alone can mislead. REMEMBER: a fused five-pleated funnel may hide the species-defining sepals on the UNDERSIDE. The old illustrated comparison plate is a concept sketch, NOT an actual measured photo strip.
shared_traits: Convolvulaceae morning glories mostly have ALTERNATE, simple, long-stalked leaves, typically lack STIPULES and climb by TWINING stems rather than tendrils. Leaf blades may be heart-shaped or 3–7-lobed even within one species.
The corolla comprises FIVE fused petals making a funnel or narrow tube, with five folds/creases and mid-petal zones; a whole corolla is ONE flower, unlike a sunflower HEAD.
Five free or mostly free persistent SEPALS form the CALYX outside and beneath the corolla. Their lengths, shapes, protruding tips and HAIRS are often more diagnostic than the large flower face.

The species have a superior ovary that typically matures into a dry CAPSULE with a few seeds; the sepals often persist around it. Mature fruit dimensions and seed surface are useful for lacunosa-complex hybrids.
Ipomoea coccinea differs markedly in red small salverform flowers and hornlike sepal appendages, while batatas is a crop/escape comparison and must not be used as a native-field anchor.

genus_diagnostics.corolla: A COROLLA is the entire fused petal tube/funnel with its broad limb; a corolla has five folded or pleated sectors (plicate), often showing mid-petaline stripes. Measure its LENGTH in side view from base to rim; frontal WIDTH alone is not comparable to source descriptions.
genus_diagnostics.calyx: A CALYX comprises five GREEN SEPALS below the corolla, often still visible around the fruit. Outer sepals and inner sepals can differ in length, hair and apex; inspect both. Do not call the green sepals separate petals or the flower stalk a sepal.
genus_diagnostics.sepals: Short ~6–7 mm sepal group = triloba. Intermediate ~8–14 mm with lanceolate outer sepals and variable ciliate hairs = cordatotriloba. Long abruptly narrowed/recurved tips (12–24 mm) = hederacea. Long gradually tapered, often densely hairy sepals = nil. Longer 18–30 mm hairy sepals + very large flowers = lindheimeri. Differences overlap; photograph BOTH sepals and a ruler.
genus_diagnostics.leaf: ALTERNATE leaves emerge singly from the stem nodes, not in opposite pairs; a long PETIOLE connects a leaf blade to the twining stem. Cordate = heart-shaped base, palmate lobes = lobes radiate out from petiole insertion, and hairs may occur across blade and margins. Three-lobed leaves do NOT distinguish hederacea from nil, triloba or cordatotriloba.
genus_diagnostics.sepal_hairs: PUBESCENCE means fine hairs; CILIATE means fringe hairs along the SEPAL MARGINS; HISPID means coarse/bristly hairs. Hederacea calyx is conspicuously hairy with abruptly long sepal tips; nil can ALSO have a very hairy calyx, so use taper shape + flowering size rather than hair presence alone.
genus_diagnostics.flower_stalk: A PEDUNCLE supports a whole flower cluster; a PEDICEL supports one flower. Coccinea fruiting pedicels can REFLEX (bend backward/downward) and its sepals have short hornlike/awnlike CORNIFORM appendages; both need a flower/fruit side macro.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Fruit is generally a CAPSULE that opens when ripe; persistent sepals may surround its base. Lacunosa ~10–13 mm fruit, and hybrids I. ×leucantha with cordatotriloba can be intermediate; record mature capsule and measured seeds when flowers have weathered.
genus_diagnostics.roots: Annual twining herbs such as hederacea, nil and triloba differ from perennials such as lindheimeri and many cordatotriloba plants; batatas is distinctive for enlarged STORAGE ROOTS and cultivated/sprawling crop habit. Do not infer root structure from a leafy face photo.
genus_diagnostics.habit: Most twine by wrapping the actual STEM around a support, unlike Passiflora which uses TENDRILS. Batatas often TRAILS and does not need to climb; leaf shape and flower color vary by crop/escape lineage.

comparison_cards.title: Littlebell versus tie-vine (triloba / cordatotriloba)
comparison_cards.look_here_first: MEASURE flowers from the side: littlebell corollas usually 10–20 mm and sepals ~6–7 mm; tie-vine usually ~20–38 mm with outer/inner sepals ~8–14 mm. Both can carry three-lobed leaves, so leaf shape is a trap. FNA triloba is introduced; cordatotriloba native-status is tracked independently.
photo_requirements: paired photo side views with common ruler showing the fresh corolla base and rim
calyx underside of both species with sepal tips and hair margins resolved
comparison_cards.caution: The front-facing physical images show the trumpet, not a reliably measurable flower/sepal comparison; var. cordatotriloba remains represented in species without duplicate card.

comparison_cards.title: Ivy-leaf versus Japanese morning-glory (hederacea / nil)
comparison_cards.look_here_first: SEPAL TIP: hederacea sepals narrow ABRUPTLY into long curved/recurved or spreading terminal portions; nil's long, bristly hairy sepals are generally more GRADUALLY tapered/straighter. Both may be 3-lobed-leaved and bluish or purple. Use whole flower size as backup, not hairs alone.
photo_requirements: matched same-scale FRESH side-on sepal pairs, no detached petal blocking

comparison_cards.title: Whitestar versus hybrid morning-glory (lacunosa / ×leucantha / cordatotriloba)
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Lacunosa usually has smaller WHITE funnel flowers and ~11–14 mm acuminate sepals. Pink/lavender cordatotriloba is larger on average; BUT I. ×leucantha hybrid can be intermediate. Compare measured mature capsules/seed lengths and overall morphology.
photo_requirements: lacunosa and cordatotriloba flowers and calyx at same scale
fruit diameters and seeds with mm scale
do not invent a new hybrid species entry or native metrics
comparison_cards.caution: White flower alone is not sufficient, and some local photo sets are private study or horticultural context.

comparison_cards.title: Scarlet versus other red morning-glories (coccinea / hederifolia)
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Small red/orange corolla is a first glance, not a definitive species diagnosis. Verify distinctive hornlike CORNIFORM appendages at sepal tips and backward/reflexed PEDICELS when fruits mature.
photo_requirements: calyx corniform tooth macro with mm scale
fruiting pedicel clearly reflexed on the SAME stem
side comparison with I. hederifolia sourced separately
comparison_cards.caution: I. hederifolia is an outside-module look-alike; do not count as installed canonical species.

comparison_cards.title: Lindheimer versus nil versus sweet potato
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Lindheimer's very large bluish funnel plus hairy 3–7-lobed leaves suggests a perennial morning-glory. Nil also has hairy 3-lobed leaves but long different sepal tips and generally smaller flowers. Batatas is a crop/escape with STORAGE ROOTS and trailing habit; a crop leaf image alone proves neither native status nor roots.
photo_requirements: Lindheimer flower side + sepal + ruler, paired nil comparison
same-plant sweet-potato root + flowering vine macro
distinguish perennial rootstock from cultivated tuberous roots
comparison_cards.caution: I. batatas remains a project native-range FAIL; do not promote by genus group membership.
